headline: Open access through the Glen Nevis valley
reservation: Entry to the falls and gorge does not currently require a formal reservation system or permit. Hikers should check official John Muir Trust updates for any temporary path maintenance closures or local access restrictions before heading into the Nevis area.

days.title: Steall Gorge and the Nevis Waterfalls

stops.name: Steall Falls
stops.detail: Hike the two-mile rocky route through the dramatic Steall Gorge to reach the 100-metre plunge of An Steall Bàn. Adventurous visitors may choose to use the wire bridge to cross the River Nevis near the base of the falls.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to reach the glen trailhead; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: The terrain is described as wild and rocky; ensure a pace that accounts for uneven footing in the gorge.

intel.title: Glen Nevis Access
intel.text: Evidence does not specify exact parking capacity or fill times at the trailhead. Visitors should verify local parking availability in Glen Nevis before arrival.

intel.title: Cellular Service
intel.text: Connectivity in the deep gorge and mountain shadows is not documented in official sources. Expect potential gaps in service and carry navigation backups.

intel.title: Local Supplies
intel.text: No fuel or services are noted within the Steall Gorge area. Reliable supply points are typically located in the nearby gateway of Fort William.

intel.title: Trail Pacing
intel.text: The walk is approximately two miles long through a rocky gorge. Allow several hours to safely navigate the meadows and river crossing.

intel.title: Path Conditions
intel.text: The route is characterized as wild and rocky. Heavy rainfall can affect the River Nevis water levels and the feasibility of using the wire bridge.

plan.arrival: Pick up supplies in Fort William before driving into Glen Nevis; check-in at local accommodation prior to the trailhead departure.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the road to Glen Nevis, though visitors should check for any seasonal road restrictions in the Highlands.
plan.goldenHour: Steall Falls at sunset, where light hits the 100-metre drop, depending on seasonal sun angles.
